races.name: Irish EBF Auction Series Race (IRE Incentive Race)
BOYLE Sports Money Back If 2nd To SP Fav Handicap

runners_data.name: Faoladh
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner here; won over 7f Good at Leopardstown in April so the course-and-distance form ticks, though six months off that peak and a crowded prominent division makes maintaining a clean lead likely; 7lb claimer Adam Browne-Souza takes the mount with a modest 14-day trainer strike rate.

runners_data.name: Buttermere Ridge
runners_data.note: 234 days off the track is a major concern for a horse who has failed to place in five runs and fades in finishes; hold-up style is genuinely a disadvantage in a race likely to be run at a steady pace, and soft/heavy going form does not transfer well to Good.

runners_data.name: Perfect Base
runners_data.note: Two-year-old rated 71, ran five times last season with two places over 7-8f on Good — the distance and going suit — but 262 days off track and a trainer without a 14-day winner in seven attempts makes the return on trust a leap of faith.

runners_data.name: Send Harry
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer who has placed five times in his last five runs and previously won over 7f at the Curragh; 30 days since last run is fine, and the 7f Good conditions match two of his five historical starts well — one of the most likely to actually secure a handy berth ahead of the pack.

runners_data.name: Apache Outlaw
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up type who has not placed on Good going at a comparable distance (7/15 sim-going, 0W1P); trainer McGuinness has two wins from 24 in 14 days which is active, but this horse's best form has come on faster surfaces and at shorter.

runners_data.name: Ardeur
runners_data.note: Long-absent hold-up runner (71 days) whose recent form includes finishes of 15th and 15th; the Good-ground record is sparse (3/9 sim-going, 1W1P) and at 8f rather than 7f, making this trip a slight concern — needs a truly strong pace to get into contention which this race shape is unlikely to provide.

runners_data.name: Phoenix Pairc
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Good (Curragh, STA), so the distance and going profile is genuine; 181 days off is the critical negative, but the hold-up style means he needs a stronger-than-expected pace to deliver late, and he must produce a career-best return from a long break.

runners_data.name: Reposado
runners_data.note: Consistent placer at 5-6f, stepping up to 7f here which is at the outer limit of his winning form; races prominently and is likely to secure a forward position given his recent good handicap form (six of last six all placed or close up), but the trip extension is a risk.

runners_data.name: Loingseoir
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran who placed in two of his last three over 7f on Soft, but the Leopardstown Good surface produced only a 7th in eight outings; raced just seven days ago and at 68 OR still runs off a workable mark — a prominent type who may find the 7f Good less suitable than his Soft efforts suggest.

runners_data.name: Navagio
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who has not placed in a 7f or 8f Good race in 15 comparable starts (0W0P sim-going); recent form shows a string of mid-table finishes and the hold-up style needs a strong pace — unlikely to get one here — making a winning run implausible.

runners_data.name: Free Solo
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran, two wins and two places from 15 on similar going — the form is patchy but present; races prominently using a tongue strap and blinkers, but finishing positions of 0-0-7-11-13 in the last five runs suggest he is not at his peak, and Ben Coen's booking is the positive note.

runners_data.name: Goal Exceeded
runners_data.note: McGuinness's second string here with three wins from 22 in 14 days; placed twice at 7f and won at that trip on Soft, and the Soft/Heavy placing at 7f on Slow/Soft Good ground gives some sim-going confidence — one of the more plausible prominent types to secure a forward berth and deliver in a steady-pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Mickey The Steel
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner or prominent racer in true race conditions, but with the prominent positions already contested by several rivals, this 8yo is likely to find himself shuffled into a less comfortable midfield spot; recent form shows a 3rd and 2nd at 6f which encourages, though 7f and Good at Leopardstown are slightly outside his comfort zone.

runners_data.name: Hexagonal
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who has placed at 8-10f Good with two places from ten on similar going; the redistribution to midfield means he is likely to be closer than his natural style dictates — still a true closer who needs gaps to open, and the steady pace this race implies makes his task harder than the map position suggests.

runners_data.name: Irish Rumour
runners_data.note: Four places from 15 on similar going including two at 7f Good, and held form figures at this distance; a natural prominent racer who is likely to be pressed back into mid-division given the crowded front-running contingent — if he does secure a forward berth his course form (2nd over 6f Good Leopardstown) makes him a legitimate player.

runners_data.name: Caffu Zafeen
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a remarkable record of six finishes in consecutive positions (6-6-6-6-6) in recent form — no win or place in 17 starts on comparable Going (0W2P); the redistribution to midfield is academic given the pattern of finishing in the same spot regardless of position; a pace scenario that suits closers would still need a significant step forward from this horse.

runners_data.name: Eichan San
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who has shown some ability at 6f Good (5th Curragh) but the step to 7f and the move to Leopardstown are untested in his recent campaign; a front-running type by nature who will be competing for space in an already crowded prominent division, and with 0W0P on comparable going the evidence for a positive outcome here is thin.

races.paceDynamic: Faoladh is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with just one horse willing to lead in a field of 17, is set to control this race from the front at a sustainable, unflustered gallop — a genuine soft lead over 7f at Leopardstown on Good ground. The prominent contingent is overcrowded: Mickey The Steel, Irish Rumour, Eichan San, Send Harry, Reposado, Perfect Base, Loingseoir, Free Solo and Goal Exceeded all want to race handy, but the map cannot accommodate them all, meaning several will be shuffled back into unfamiliar midfield territory and will race out of role. This field holds significantly more front-running and prominent types than can realistically secure their position — of those, Send Harry, Reposado and Goal Exceeded are most likely to press Faoladh and actually achieve a prominent berth, given their recent form and distance profiles. A controlled, single-paced gallop with a moderate early tempo favours horses who can race prominently in the first four or five and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs, rather than hold-up runners who will be trapped in traffic with insufficient room and pace to exploit late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Faoladh Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Faoladh sets a steady, uncontested lead and the race develops as a sustained-gallop contest with the pace controlled from the front.
scenarios.body: If Faoladh sets a steady, uncontested lead and the race develops as a sustained-gallop contest with the pace controlled from the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stalkers Pounce At Two Out
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is truly moderate and horses held just off the pace in third to sixth accelerate sharply when the winner kicks turning in.
scenarios.body: If the early gallop is truly moderate and horses held just off the pace in third to sixth accelerate sharply when the winner kicks turning in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Weave Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If a pocket of mid-race pace injection — triggered by Send Harry or Reposado pressing Faoladh — strings the field out and creates gaps for runners coming from sixth to tenth.
scenarios.body: If a pocket of mid-race pace injection — triggered by Send Harry or Reposado pressing Faoladh — strings the field out and creates gaps for runners coming from sixth to tenth.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Deep Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is fast enough to drain Faoladh and the prominent pack, gifting the race to runners who were pushed to the rear involuntarily.
scenarios.body: If the early tempo is fast enough to drain Faoladh and the prominent pack, gifting the race to runners who were pushed to the rear involuntarily.

watchPoints.text: Faoladh (sole front-runner) has 17 rivals and a crowded prominent pack behind — if Send Harry or Reposado press hard from the gates, the effective lead margin collapses and the race tempo could rise sharply, transforming the shape entirely.

Mickey The Steel, Irish Rumour and Eichan San are all natural front-runners likely to be denied their position at the start — watch for scrimmaging and barging in the first furlong as multiple horses fight for the same territory along the rail.

Goal Exceeded's trainer Adrian McGuinness has three winners from 22 runners in the past 14 days in this field — stable is in form and this horse's 7f placing record at a workable OR warrants close monitoring in the market before the off.

Phoenix Pairc and Hexagonal, both true hold-up types, return from 181 and 8 days respectively — neither will benefit from the anticipated steady pace, but if the tempo unexpectedly quickens mid-race they are the horses most likely to finish through late and catch the eye without winning.

Buttermere Ridge (234 days off) and Perfect Base (262 days off) represent major unknown quantities on fitness grounds — significant market moves for either would be the only reason to reconsider their low probability of landing a place.

races.name: Bulmers Live Handicap

runners_data.name: Local Lad
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for Gerard O'Leary, 60 days off and returning to a trip short of his recent 10f assignments; Good-ground form is modest (0 wins, 2 places from 9 similar runs) and he will need luck from deep in an 18-runner field to get involved.

runners_data.name: Zaraahmando
runners_data.note: Prominent-travelling type with a win on soft and two places from six similar-going efforts; Jimmy Dalton (7lb) keeps the weight handy, and a recent 25-day break suits a horse that tends to run well fresh — the mile on Good here is squarely in his wheelhouse.

runners_data.name: Heliogabalus
runners_data.note: Shane Foley takes the mount for Mrs Harrington on a horse who won over course and distance on Good last season; the 269-day absence is the single biggest question mark, but the trainer has a solid 10/45 strike rate over 14 days and this horse's course form reads well if fit.

runners_data.name: Bucaneer's Spirit
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent runner with two wins over 8f on Good, has run well in similar company recently and comes back from just 8 days ago in good order; the Good surface and straightforward mile profile suit him well, and stable form (2/16 over 14 days) is acceptable.

runners_data.name: Smithfield
runners_data.note: Prominent type for Gavin Cromwell that has shown flashes at 8f on Good (1 place from 7 similar-going runs) but has been inconsistent; 21 days since last run is fine, though the form string of 870-40 over this trip does not inspire confidence at this level.

runners_data.name: Battle Borne
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose best form has come on Standside and soft tracks rather than Good ground; the form figure of 0 wins and 0 places from 15 similar-going runs is a significant negative flag, and the wide draw in a big field complicates matters further.

runners_data.name: Go Out
runners_data.note: Prominent runner that has been running consistently over shorter trips (6-7f) and steps up in distance here; zero wins from 11 Good-ground runs over 8f is a concern, though McDonogh's booking adds tactical intelligence if he can find a good position.

runners_data.name: Bay Of Dreams
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner or prominent racer by inclination, but with the field saturated by similar types, Ben Coen is unlikely to get him anywhere near his preferred position; his best form came when bowling along up front (two 2nds on Good), so the compromised role dents his claims here.

runners_data.name: Perfect Judgement
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for P J F Murphy with a pattern of finishing 7th in Good-ground contests; 8 days since last run and 0 wins from 15 similar-going efforts make it hard to make a case, even if the pace develops in his favour.

runners_data.name: Ocean Echo
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3yo who was second over 7f at Naas on Heavy and has limited Good-ground evidence; Paddy Harnett (5lb) takes over for Mark Fahey and the step up to a mile is unexplored — interesting projection but unproven at this level over this trip.

runners_data.name: Running Point
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will be allowed a soft lead with no rivals pressing, giving Chris Hayes the chance to dictate fractions; the STYLE_FIT tag reflects that his form when genuinely challenged or on a target trip is modest, but unchallenged on the front end he becomes a live player.

runners_data.name: Fleetfootsoldier
runners_data.note: Burns's 6yo has shown prominent tendencies throughout his career, yet the surplus of pace in this field means Nicola Burns (5lb) will struggle to park him where he wants to be; form of 9 wins and 0 places from 15 similar-going runs at 8f underlines how far off his best this trip and surface have found him.

runners_data.name: Navajo Point
runners_data.note: Returning after 402 days off for Martin Hassett, and the flag for fading in the finish is concerning on such a flat, one-mile track; genuine hold-up style but bumped to a midfield mapping, and the long absence makes it very hard to assess his current condition.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Funk
runners_data.note: Consistent 3yo for G M Lyons who has a placed effort over 8f on Good and is dropping back from 10f; Gary Carroll is an astute jockey in big-field handicaps and this horse's profile — prominent, course-experienced, fit (14 days) — makes him a realistic candidate if the pace unfolds steadily.

runners_data.name: Verhoyen
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old hold-up specialist with two places from 15 similar-going runs; Jack Cleary (5lb) can't fully compensate for the age and modest recent form, and though the REDISTRIBUTED tag means he may get closer than expected positionally, genuine impact seems unlikely.

runners_data.name: Sayfa Fad
runners_data.note: Returning from 261 days off with a fade-in-finish flag and a hold-up style pushed closer to midfield than natural; the one win on Good is a positive but the layoff and finishing pattern on this flat track are difficult to overcome in a competitive 18-runner handicap.

runners_data.name: Dawn Flame
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Paul Flynn that fades in the finish and has limited Good-ground evidence over 8f; Leigh Roche takes the ride but the form string (-81490) is inconsistent and the combination of a big field, a flag for weakening, and modest similar-going form is off-putting.

runners_data.name: Millhone
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up or patient-ridden horse who has been mapped out of his preferred deep-lying role by the sheer weight of rear-end traffic in this field; Rory Mulligan (5lb) inherits a compromised ride and the form (0 wins, 0 places on Good at 8f from 5 runs) leaves little to work with.

races.paceDynamic: Running Point is the sole confirmed front-runner in an 18-runner field and, with no genuine rival pressing for the lead, should be able to dictate a controlled, honest gallop on Good ground over the mile at Leopardstown. That sustainable tempo is unlikely to produce the searching end-to-end gallop that burns off prominent types, meaning horses racing just behind the leader — Zaraahmando, Bucaneer's Spirit, Smithfield, Cosmic Funk and Ocean Echo — will enjoy a relatively undemanding trip and be primed to challenge early in the straight. The field contains more natural front-running and prominent types than can physically hold those positions: Bay Of Dreams, Fleetfootsoldier and Millhone are genuine prominent or prominent-leaning horses who have been mapped away from the front and are unlikely to secure their natural berths, so their effectiveness is compromised. This race shape — a single steady pace-setter, a compressed midfield, and a controlled tempo — firmly favours prominent-to-mid-division horses who can sit close to the action without burning energy and produce a sustained one-paced finish rather than hold-up closers depending on a strong pace to pull them through.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Running Point sets a steady tempo and the first two home emerge from the prominent group immediately behind him.
scenarios.body: If Running Point sets a steady tempo and the first two home emerge from the prominent group immediately behind him.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Running Point is allowed a soft lead throughout and the pace is too modest to bring the field to him.
scenarios.body: If Running Point is allowed a soft lead throughout and the pace is too modest to bring the field to him.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinder Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just honest enough to draw the field together and a horse from mid-division arrives with a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: If the pace is just honest enough to draw the field together and a horse from mid-division arrives with a sustained late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is surprisingly quick early — perhaps through jostling among the prominent contingent — and the field comes back to hold-up horses in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the pace is surprisingly quick early — perhaps through jostling among the prominent contingent — and the field comes back to hold-up horses in the final furlong.

watchPoints.text: Running Point (Chris Hayes) will attempt to dictate from the front unchallenged — if he is allowed a completely uncontested lead, he will set a falsely slow pace that leaves the field bunched and hold-up horses with nowhere to go in the straight.

Bay Of Dreams and Fleetfootsoldier are natural prominent racers who cannot get their preferred position in an 18-runner field; watch for both to race keenly in an unnatural midfield slot early, which could see them burn energy and fade late when they need it most.

Heliogabalus returns after 269 days off — if he shows any signs of race-rustiness or greenness in the Leopardstown straight, his big market move (if any) should be treated with caution despite strong course-and-distance form.

With 18 runners on a flat mile at Leopardstown, the draw and early positioning will be critical — horses drawn wide who get stuck three or four wide throughout the race will cover significantly more ground, particularly those redistributed to midfield who cannot find an inside berth.

Navajo Point (402 days off) and Sayfa Fad (261 days off) are the two longest-absent runners in the field; both carry a fades-in-finish flag and hold-up styles mapped away from their natural positions — watch for them to be non-factors unless each trainer has given exceptional work at home.

races.name: BOYLE Sports Home Of The Early Payout Rated Race

runners_data.name: God Of Power
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner whose entire race plan revolves around dictating from the front; won last time over 7f on Good and is proven at a mile, but the STYLE_FIT flag is a mild caution given he is operating on the edge of his comfort zone stepping to 1m with a field of prominent types pressing him.|

runners_data.name: Shaftesbury Avenue
runners_data.note: A P O'Brien's charge arrives on 32 days' rest with a win at The Heathcare over 8f on Heavier ground; this is his first run on Good since a 6th at the Curragh and the step back in going is a key unknown, though Jack Cleary claims 5lb on the prominent racer.|

runners_data.name: Sir Benji
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell drops this one back from 10f to 1m having won over 10f on Heavy at Naas; the step up in class is the query, but Robert Whearty takes the ride and the horse has form in two runs on Good, placing once, giving him a workable going profile.|

runners_data.name: Krasimir
runners_data.note: Gary Carroll's mount has been consistently placed in four runs on Good ground, all at sprint distances — stepping to a mile is the significant trip question, but his relentless consistency at 0W4P on this going suggests he handles conditions well and will be competitive tracking the pace.|

runners_data.name: Red Autumn
runners_data.note: D K Weld's hold-up runner has most of his form on Soft, with only one run on Good — a 5th over 8f — in his last five starts; he needs a genuinely run race to get involved from off the pace and Chris Hayes will have to be patient in the closing stages.|

runners_data.name: Golddream
runners_data.note: David Marnane's runner won over 8f at Stratford-on-Avon and has solid placed form on Good ground; he is a genuine prominent racer by nature but with several rivals ahead of him in the pecking order at the front, he has been mapped to midfield, which represents a compromise of his natural game.|

runners_data.name: Halon Bay
runners_data.note: Ciaran Murphy sends this one out fresh on 39 days' rest after a win over 7f Good at Naas; his natural inclination is to race prominently or lead, but with God Of Power and a cluster of prominent types in the way, he is unlikely to replicate that front-running role and Ben Coen will need to adapt the tactics.|

runners_data.name: Johnny Soda
runners_data.note: Adrian McGuinness's hold-up type has uneven recent form — a win over 8f Soft sandwiched between modest efforts — and is two from eight on Good or similar ground; Adam Caffrey takes the ride but this horse needs things to go his way from the rear and the race shape is unlikely to suit.|

runners_data.name: Glitter And Glory
runners_data.note: Shane Foley partners a mare whose record shows wins and places at Southwell over shorter trips on Standard, with her only Good-going runs producing a 5th and a 3rd; she is by nature a prominent or forward-racing type but is pushed back into a midfield position by the volume of similar runners, limiting her ability to reproduce her most effective style.|

races.paceDynamic: God Of Power is the one confirmed front-runner and, with a clear lead from the gates, is likely to dictate at a sensible gallop on Good ground over this straight mile at Leopardstown. Shaftesbury Avenue, Sir Benji, and Krasimir are genuine prominent types who will press up behind God Of Power and create a compact, structured early order rather than a frantic pace battle. The resulting tempo should be honest but controlled, meaning the race will be decided by a sustained gallop into the straight rather than a late sprint off a falsely slow pace — conditions that favour horses who can race handily and sustain their effort rather than pure closers. This field carries more prominent-racing types than can all secure their preferred position: Golddream, Halon Bay, and Glitter And Glory are natural front-runners or prominent horses who will be forced to settle further back than ideal, meaning their redistribution to midfield is a genuine compromise of their natural style.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: God Of Power Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If God Of Power breaks well and establishes an uncontested lead, setting a fair but unhurried gallop that only quickens from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: If God Of Power breaks well and establishes an uncontested lead, setting a fair but unhurried gallop that only quickens from the two-furlong pole.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Packers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If God Of Power leads at a genuinely even tempo and the prominent group of Krasimir, Shaftesworth Avenue, and Sir Benji travel sweetly just off the pace and deliver a collective challenge entering the straight.
scenarios.body: If God Of Power leads at a genuinely even tempo and the prominent group of Krasimir, Shaftesworth Avenue, and Sir Benji travel sweetly just off the pace and deliver a collective challenge entering the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistributed Runners Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the race is messy enough to allow Golddream, Halon Bay, or Glitter And Glory to recover something close to their natural forward position.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses or the race is messy enough to allow Golddream, Halon Bay, or Glitter And Glory to recover something close to their natural forward position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than anticipated and the front-running group burns out in the final furlong, leaving a gap for Red Autumn or Johnny Soda to close.
scenarios.body: If the pace is stronger than anticipated and the front-running group burns out in the final furlong, leaving a gap for Red Autumn or Johnny Soda to close.

watchPoints.text: God Of Power's break from the gates is the race-defining moment — if he misses the kick or is pressured immediately by Shaftesbury Avenue or Krasimir, the entire race shape changes and the controlled-pace scenario collapses.

Halon Bay and Golddream, both natural front-runners mapped to midfield, may contest for position in the early stages creating unexpected pressure on the pace even without intent — watch for a scrappy opening two furlongs.

Krasimir steps up significantly in distance having only raced over 6-7f previously; if the mile proves beyond his stamina in the final furlong, his consistent placed profile may flatline late despite tracking a sound pace throughout.

Sir Benji is dropping back from 10f to 1m for the first time — if that trip compression sharpens him up rather than finding him too short of room, he could arrive late with more energy than rivals who have been grinding since the front.|

Red Autumn's entire chance depends on pace collapse in the final furlong; with D K Weld's typically patient campaign management, note whether Chris Hayes seeks a wide outside draw to avoid traffic — any trouble in running makes this horse's remote chance even slimmer.|

races.name: 1878 At 3Arena Handicap (Div I)

runners_data.name: Shanlieve
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for David Marnane carrying 142lbs; recent form reads 8770-0 and she fades in finishes, making this big-field traffic scenario a tough ask, though her Good-going figures (3 from 5 runs) are at least not a concern.

runners_data.name: William F Browne
runners_data.note: Paul W Flynn-trained hold-up horse returning after 60 days off (13-day jockey absence noted); 140lbs burden and a fade tendency make it hard to see him getting competitive from rear in an 18-runner field, though one placed effort on similar ground offers faint hope.

runners_data.name: Lohengrin
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up type for E D Delany with a tongue-tie; form reads 0-B000 and despite a placed run on Good ground historically, he has finished in the last third of the field in every recent start and is hard to back with conviction.

runners_data.name: Max Meridius
runners_data.note: Shane Foley rides this hold-up gelding returning from 240 days off (13-day jockey absence flagged); his recent runs have all been over 16-17f so this 1m1f trip is a significant drop in distance, making his stamina reserve unclear and his chance speculative.

runners_data.name: Chipsrdown
runners_data.note: Trainer-ridden by Andrew Slattery; a genuine hold-up horse by nature (style-fit 0.92) who is placed here in midfield because the rear of the field is oversubscribed — his two recent placed efforts came on Good and Soft ground, and he arrives fresh off a 6-day turnaround, suggesting connections are bullish even if his positional compromise is a concern.

runners_data.name: Genuine Jim
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for R P Burns ridden by 5lb claimer Nicola Burns; form 97-000 with his best recent effort a seventh in similar company, and while Good ground is acceptable, he struggles to make meaningful headway from the rear in large fields.

runners_data.name: Lust
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old who is a true hold-up horse (style-fit 0.90) squeezed into a midfield slot on the map because the back of the field is simply too crowded; his most recent run showed a placed effort 13 days ago, and fade tendencies on Good ground are a recurring pattern — he needs gaps that may not come.

runners_data.name: Rampage
runners_data.note: One of only three prominent-style runners in the race; Sadhbh Tormey (7lb claimer) takes the ride for T G McCourt, and his Good-ground form and handicap marks over 8f are competitive — his chance hinges entirely on sitting close enough to Ella's Gold to pounce in the straight.

runners_data.name: Akashaa
runners_data.note: A two-year-old returning from 272 days off for Miss Natalia Lupini; genuinely a hold-up runner by profile (style-fit 0.92) placed into midfield by the map due to field congestion at the rear — significant absence and youth in an 18-runner handicap make this a very speculative runner.

runners_data.name: Pinball Wizard
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up horse for John C McConnell, also wearing a hood (hg:p); style-fit 0.93 means he is not in his natural position on this map — his placed efforts on Good ground are noted but he has been well held in recent starts and the crowded straight works against him.

runners_data.name: Limestone Red
runners_data.note: Tracey Collins sends out this hold-up type who has a hood and is returning from 90 days off; his all-weather form on Tapeta is strong (1W2P over 10f at Dundalk) but his Good-turf figures are poor — the style displacement (0.93 fit) compounds the surface question.

runners_data.name: Ella's Gold
runners_data.note: Ben Coen takes the mount for Matthew J Smith on this confirmed front-runner; she has been placed four times from five starts and arrives just 7 days after her last run, suggesting she is cherry-ripe — her ability to control this race from the front is the central tactical fact, though the style-fit tag (0.93) reflects she is not habitually a pure front-runner and may face a positional challenge if Rampage pushes up.

runners_data.name: Hieloray
runners_data.note: Three-year-old prominent runner for J S Moore returning from 241 days; Rory Cleary takes the ride and there is one placed effort at 8f on Heavy noted — the long absence is the obvious risk, but prominent style is the right profile for this race shape if fitness is there.

runners_data.name: Smooth
runners_data.note: Charles Weld-trained hold-up horse (style-fit 0.90) displaced from the rear into a midfield slot on the map; a fade tendency is flagged and recent form 007-98 over longer trips (10-12f) suggests this 1m1f trip may be on the sharp side for him.

runners_data.name: Nephin Mountain
runners_data.note: Wesley Joyce (3lb claimer) rides this three-year-old for Michael Mulvany; a genuine hold-up horse (style-fit 0.90) mapped into midfield due to field congestion — his recent runs have all been on Soft ground and this is his first try on Good turf, which is an unknown factor.

runners_data.name: Half Nutz
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran for James M Barcoe ridden by 10lb claimer E E Ryan; a true hold-up horse (style-fit 0.90) placed into midfield on the map — recent form 085853 shows consistency without winning, and at this age in an 18-runner field the positional compromise is a significant negative.

runners_data.name: Curious Jane
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up filly for Ciaran Murphy with a fade tendency flagged; style-fit 0.90 means she is not in her natural rear position — form reads 0-00 from just three runs and she is the lightest-weighted runner in the field at 120lbs, but inexperience and a 54-day break make this a developmental run at best.

runners_data.name: Jewels Legacy
runners_data.note: Jamie Powell rides this three-year-old hold-up filly for M A Cahill, who has a hood (hg:b); form 0996-0 with all runs on Good or Soft ground — fade tendency is flagged, style-fit is 0.90, and she sits in midfield on the map only because the rear is oversubscribed, not because it is her natural territory.

races.paceDynamic: Ella's Gold is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner flat handicap over 1m1f at Leopardstown, and with no genuine rivals to dispute the lead, she is set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset on Good ground. Rampage and Hieloray are the only other prominent-style runners, meaning Ella's Gold should slide into an uncontested lead without expending early energy, setting a tempo that is honest but not punishing. With the bulk of the field comprising hold-up types — many of whom (Chipsrdown, Lust, Nephin Mountain, Akashaa, Pinball Wizard, Limestone Red, Smooth, Half Nutz, Curious Jane, Jewels Legacy) are genuine rear-of-field horses redistributed into midfield on the map simply because they cannot all sit at the back — the race shape strongly favours a horse that can track the pace in second or third and quicken in the straight, as true hold-up horses will face a wall of traffic when they ask their questions. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically all get to the rear, meaning Chipsrdown and Lust are most likely to secure a position closer to the pace than their natural style suggests, though both carry style-fit discounts. This race shape decisively favours the prominent-to-midfield tracker profile — a horse that sits within two or three lengths of Ella's Gold early and has the reserves to kick past her in the final two furlongs.

watchPoints.text: Ella's Gold (Ben Coen) — watch whether she is allowed to stride on unopposed from the gates; if Rampage or Hieloray pushes up to challenge her for the lead in the first furlong, the pace dynamic changes entirely and her chance is significantly undermined.

Chipsrdown and Lust — both are genuine hold-up horses mapped into midfield due to field congestion; if they are unable to secure that midfield position at the start and drift back to their natural rear position, they face an almost impossible task in a field of 18 on a track that does not favour wide, late runs.

Hieloray — returning from 241 days off, the fitness question is real; watch the betting market and the parade ring for signs of condition, because if he is fit, his prominent style is perfectly suited to this race shape.

Traffic management in the straight — with 18 runners and a majority of hold-up horses all seeking room simultaneously in the home straight at Leopardstown, watch for a severe bunching effect; runners widest on the track in the final two furlongs (Half Nutz, Nephin Mountain on the outside) could be inadvertent beneficiaries.

Limestone Red — his all-weather form is markedly superior to his turf form, and returning from 90 days on Good ground at Leopardstown is a different test entirely; watch whether the market reflects any confidence from the Tracey Collins yard before treating him as a factor.

races.name: 1878 At 3Arena Handicap (Div II)

runners_data.name: Queen Aethelflaed
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner, with strong Good-going credentials (2W3P in similar conditions); maps as Prominent but is effectively the pace-setter here, and her chance rises sharply if she can get away uncontested — her STYLE_FIT tag reflects she is racing outside her usual role only in that she may lead rather than track.

runners_data.name: Deuteronomy
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old prominent racer with wins at this 10f-equivalent trip on Good ground; T14 return of 0/2 is uninspiring but the horse has finished 1st and 8th in recent Good-ground starts, suggesting consistency in ideal conditions — a prime candidate to track the leader and challenge.

runners_data.name: Rockbury Lad
runners_data.note: Prominent type who showed a placed effort at 8f on Tapeta recently, but Good-ground form over slightly shorter is his best work; trainer O'Callaghan firing well (T14: 2/9) and the switch back to turf on Good going could suit — one to respect from the front of the chasing pack.

runners_data.name: Medieval Night
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a persistent fading pattern (tagged ⚠), finishing in the 8-11 range across most recent starts on Good and Soft; the 17-day break and OR of 57 give marginal scope, but a true test of stamina would be needed for this profile and the expected controlled pace does not provide it.

runners_data.name: Sheamus Seimhiu
runners_data.note: Absent for 234 days and lacking any Good-going win or place in recent history (0W0P); a hold-up runner who fades late, and a return from a lengthy lay-off in a field this competitive makes engagement here speculative at best.

runners_data.name: Staywitherjohnny
runners_data.note: Hold-up type without the fade flag to the same extent as others, with a placed effort at 9f on Soft and a decent 3rd at 8f on Good; Shane Foley's booking is a positive and the horse has shown some tenacity in the finish — if the pace quickens and traffic opens, a live place chance from midfield.

runners_data.name: Famous Enough
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a Good-going win to his name (1/8f/GOO) and consistent placing in similar conditions; T14 rate of 1/6 is acceptable and 44 days since last run is not a concern — travels close enough to the pace to be dangerous if the gallop is steady and he can kick at the two-furlong pole.

runners_data.name: Real Petite
runners_data.note: Genuinely interesting profile — a hold-up horse who won over 8f on Good ground and whose fading tag may reflect step-ups in trip rather than a structural weakness; 6 days since last run is fine, and a return to 9f on Good could see her finish more strongly than the hold-up tag implies.

runners_data.name: Virgil Tibbs
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type absent 225 days with a fade flag and no win or place in similar going (0W0P at sim-going 4/7); the long break and weak pace record make this a very tough assignment in a competitive handicap.

runners_data.name: Nibras Rainbow
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner with a recent Good-ground win (1/8f/GOO) and active form (LR: 7d); the visor is a headgear flag worth noting and trainer Flynn has been busy (T14: 3/24) — a lively each-way contender if he secures a tracking position early.

runners_data.name: Sarmiento Power
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse in terms of true running style, placed in midfield on the map because the field is saturated with closers; his form in Good conditions is almost non-existent (sim-going: 1/15) and his recent runs have been over much longer trips — the distance drop and going make this a difficult ask.

runners_data.name: Shakita
runners_data.note: True hold-up type shifted to midfield representation due to the volume of closers in the field; all recent form comes over 13f-16f on Good, Soft and Heavy, making this 9f trip on Good ground a significant undertrip — the style fit (0.90) and form profile make this highly speculative.

runners_data.name: Crypto Crash
runners_data.note: Lengthy 315-day absence and all recent form over extreme distances of 16f-20f; mapped to midfield because of redistribution from the hold-up cluster, but this is fundamentally a staying type dropped sharply in trip who has not raced in nearly a year — conditions are stacked against.

runners_data.name: Private Larry
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up operator whose best sim-going effort reads as 1/5, sitting in midfield on the map only because there is no room for more closers at the rear; three-year-old with modest recent form, and the step up to 9f here on Good ground is a new test — the style fit (0.90) reflects the challenge.

runners_data.name: Desert Of The Sea
runners_data.note: Consistent performer on AW (multiple places at 7-8f on Tapeta) who maps to midfield via redistribution rather than by natural inclination — a true hold-up type; the 90-day gap and switch to turf on Good ground are concerns, but the placed form is genuine if conditions ever suit.

runners_data.name: Yquem
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse mapped into midfield through redistribution; best form has come at 10f on Tapeta, and the fade flag plus absence of any turf win in recent history (sim-going: 4/9) raises doubts about whether Good turf over 9f unlocks anything new.

runners_data.name: Borora Aura
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old with unknown running style (U); two placed efforts at 10f on Good ground suggest stamina and some ability, and Wesley Joyce's 3lb claim adds appeal — the unexposed profile and trainer Mulvany's T14 record of 2/11 make this worth including in wider calculations.

races.paceDynamic: Queen Aethelflaed is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 17-runner field and, with no genuine challenger likely to press her hard from the off, she should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m1f Leopardstown flat on Good ground. The prominent-racing contingent of Deuteronomy, Rockbury Lad, Famous Enough and Nibras Rainbow will sit just behind her, tracking the pace without forcing it into a true test, meaning the tempo is unlikely to be anything more than honest. Several horses labelled as hold-up types — Private Larry, Sarmiento Power, Shakita, Crypto Crash, Desert Of The Sea and Yquem — are redistributed to midfield because this crowded field cannot accommodate them all at the rear; the horses most likely to actually secure a prominent tracking position are Deuteronomy, Rockbury Lad and Famous Enough, who have the profile and draw advantage to do so. With a single uncontested pacemaker and a moderate tempo, this race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently just off the pace — those able to travel close to Queen Aethelflaed and kick from the front of the chasing pack will have the clearest route and will not need to weave through traffic off a slow early pace.

watchPoints.text: Queen Aethelflaed — if she jumps cleanly and is not pressed in the first two furlongs, she could establish a lead that proves very difficult to peg back on this flat track with no other confirmed front-runner in the field.

Deuteronomy and Famous Enough — both prominent racers in a field of 17 where early position will be contested; if either gets squeezed out on the first bend they will likely underperform their map position.

Sarmiento Power, Private Larry and Shakita are all mapped to midfield via redistribution but are true hold-up types — if punters back them expecting a strong late run, note they are unlikely to get back far enough for that run to materialise given the redistribution.

Borora Aura — the unexposed three-year-old with an unknown running style and a useful apprentice claim; if she settles well and the field does compress mid-race, she could emerge as a dark horse, particularly if her stamina for 9f proves superior to lightly exposed rivals.

Real Petite — despite the hold-up tag and fade flag, her win came over 8f on Good and her placed effort over the same trip suggests the fade may be trip-related; worth monitoring in-running to see if she travels more powerfully than recent outings imply.

races.name: BOYLE Sports Squad Builder (Q.R.) Maiden

runners_data.name: Certamen
runners_data.note: Five-year-old whose recent record over similar Good-ground trips (five runs, no win, no place) is uninspiring; jockey claim (7lb) and 45-day jumps absence add doubt, and though a genuine hold-up horse at heart, the volume of closers in this field means it is likely to find itself tracking midfield rather than off the back.

runners_data.name: Chain Of Destiny
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with a fading profile in recent form (0-for-9 on Good, a finisher of 5th/9th/6th/9th/13th), and the ⚠ fade warning is consistent with its profile; this hold-up type will end up in midfield rather than the rear, but neither position looks to suit given the controlled pace expected.

runners_data.name: Donnrua Dream
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old prominent racer who has a question mark over one of its five recorded runs at this sort of trip on Good ground; a tongue tie is noted and Ray Hackett's 0/5 in 14 days is modest, but the prominent style at least puts it in the right part of the field for this race shape.

runners_data.name: Eagle Fang
runners_data.note: Lightly raced over extreme distances (19f-24f) and returning from a 1,090-day absence; the blinkers are a significant headgear flag on comeback, and while two placing runs at 24f on Good are on the form card, the significant drop in trip and the long absence make this a watch-and-see runner.

runners_data.name: Joe Cool
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a win over 16f on Good ground and two second-place finishes from five runs, making him one of the stronger form profiles in this field; prominent style suits the expected race shape well, though a 68-day absence for Noel Meade's yard (2/20 in 14 days) tempers confidence slightly.

runners_data.name: Lauro's Legend
runners_data.note: Six-year-old whose best form has come at 16f on Good, though the ⚠ fade flag and two incomplete run records raise questions; the hold-up preference and 74-day jumps gap are concerns, and this horse is not naturally positioned to capitalise on the expected prominent-led race shape.

runners_data.name: Mart Lane
runners_data.note: Five-year-old prominent racer from Barry Connell's yard who has five consecutive runs at 16f on Soft without winning — the step up to 1m7f on Good is a distinct change of scenario; 73-day absence and no Good-ground form in the history makes the conditions an unknown for this runner.

runners_data.name: Must Meet Cecil
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up type whose Good-ground form shows consistent placings (four out of 15 starts) without a win; P G Fahey's 0/2 in 14 days is modest but the horse's genuine staying profile at least gives it a chance if the pace quickens unexpectedly late.

runners_data.name: The Banger Doyle
runners_data.note: Veteran ten-year-old returning from a 308-day absence; naturally a hold-up horse with five placings from 15 Good/similar runs but no wins, the long layoff combined with the crowded back-end dynamics means it is unlikely to reproduce its best even if conditions suit.

runners_data.name: Beir Bua
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two wins and three places from six Good-ground outings, including a win over the 1m6f-1m8f band — this is one of the strongest form profiles in the race; Andrew Slattery's 4/28 in 14 days is a decent trainer stat and the prominent style sits perfectly in the expected race shape.

runners_data.name: Faerie Tales
runners_data.note: Two-year-old with just two runs, both poor (13th and 17th on Good ground at shorter trips), making this a significant ask in an 18-runner field over 1m7f; the ⚠ fade flag reinforces that this hold-up type has shown nothing yet to suggest competitive involvement.

runners_data.name: Fraher Field
runners_data.note: Six-year-old prominent racer with a win at 1m6f on Good and four placings from eight Good-ground starts — solid, consistent form profile; 17-day jumps absence is not a major concern and the prominent style is ideally aligned with what this race shape is likely to reward.

runners_data.name: Gaoth Chuil
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old whose best form comes over 20f-22f (three placings on Good/Soft), so the 1m7f trip may be on the short side; a genuine hold-up type who will end up in midfield given the cluster of closers, and that repositioning reduces its chance in the anticipated race shape.

runners_data.name: Golden Fascination
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with no recorded form data, UNKNOWN going preference, and lightly raced flag — this is a pure unknown quantity; Cian Collins's 2/14 in 14 days is noted, but there is no basis for a meaningful style or suitability assessment.

runners_data.name: Kaleo Ametsa
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up type with tongue tie and five consecutive top-9 finishes on Good ground without a win or place; the Good-ground form reads as consistent mid-division at best, and the 35-day jumps absence does not alter an underwhelming overall picture.

runners_data.name: Kimy
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up type with one win at 16f on Good and two places from 15 similar-going starts, carrying a hood (headgear); trainer Thomas Mullins has 1/5 in 14 days and while Kimy's profile suits a scenario where the pace collapses, the controlled tempo expected here limits its opportunity.

runners_data.name: Salsinha
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with two wins from six Good-ground starts at around 16f — steps up in trip here but the Good-going flag is consistent; De Bromhead's 11/39 in 14 days is the standout trainer statistic, and with no challenger for the lead, Salsinha has the opportunity to run its own race throughout, though the style-fit note (0.90) is worth bearing in mind if rivals close.

runners_data.name: Wonderwalk
runners_data.note: Three-year-old returning from 340 days off (271 days since a jumps run), with form reading as a mid-division finisher on Good ground without a win; the ⚠ fade flag and hood headgear suggest a horse that struggles to sustain its effort, and the long absence makes this very hard to assess with confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Salsinha is the confirmed lone front-runner and, with Henry De Bromhead's runner likely to stride on from the gates over this 1m7f on Good ground, the pace should be honest but entirely controllable — no rival is likely to seriously pressure for the lead. The prominent brigade of Beir Bua, Fraher Field, Joe Cool, Donnrua Dream, Eagle Fang and Mart Lane will track closely, creating a well-structured convoy behind a single pace-setter rather than a fractious battle, which typically rewards horses with tactical speed who can sit just off the lead and respond turning in. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Certamen, The Banger Doyle, Gaoth Chuil and Wonderwalk are genuine closers but are likely to find themselves mapping into midfield rather than their natural position, meaning the back end of this field is more congested and competitive than it appears on paper. The tactical verdict is clear: horses racing prominently just off Salsinha — particularly those with a track record of finishing strongly from the second or third position — are best placed in this shape, while true hold-up horses requiring a strong pace collapse to deliver them are at a structural disadvantage.

watchPoints.text: Beir Bua and Fraher Field are the two prominent horses with the clearest Good-ground winning form at this trip range — if either settles just off Salsinha in the first three, they are structurally perfectly placed and could dominate the finish.

Salsinha's lone front-running role means any unexpected challenger for the lead in the first half-mile could dramatically unsettle the race shape and accelerate the pace beyond sustainable levels — watch the first two furlongs for any breakaway.

Eagle Fang's 1,090-day absence and blinker application make it a significant behavioural wildcard — a horse returning after three years with headgear on for the first time in an 18-runner field could cause interference or race unpredictably in the early stages.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up types (Certamen, The Banger Doyle, Gaoth Chuil, Wonderwalk) forced into midfield means the middle of the field is likely to be congested from around the half-mile mark — horses needing a clear run from that group may find themselves blocked or checked entering the straight.

Joe Cool's 68-day absence from Noel Meade's stable (2/20 in 14 days) is worth monitoring in the market: if supported despite the layoff, it suggests stable confidence, and its win-and-place form on Good ground makes it a legitimate pace-shape beneficiary to track.
